newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's El Tesoro to start study for copper pit.
newsitem.headline: Chile's El Tesoro to start study for copper pit.

text.p: Minera El Tesoro, a Chilean/Australian joint venture, will start a feasibility study this year for a 60,000 tonne copper mine at its deposit in the northern Atacama Desert, said officials.
"We have a very attractive project which we hope to develop in a way which maximizes the scheme's profitability for the partners," said board president Jean Paul Luksic in a statement.
El Tesoro, one of a crop of medium-sized pits being developed in northern Chile, is owned 61 percent by Chile's Luksic group with Equatorial Mining holding 39 percent.
The mine will produce copper cathodes using the low-cost heapleaching process and is due to come on stream towards the end of 1998.
Equatorial officials had said previously that initial output at the mine would be scaled back to 30,000 tonnes to make it easier to finance the project.
